LESSON: CREATING AND

Grade: PP1
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: MUSICAL
Topic 11.1: Creating and

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Creating and. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Creating and means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Creating and from Kenya
3. practise Creating and in clear steps
4. apply Creating and in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CREATING AND
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Creating and helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: CREATING AND
Study Creating and like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Creating and means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Creating and means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Creating and means in simple pupil language.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Creating and” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Creating and means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Creating and from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Creating and from Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Creating and from Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Creating and in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Creating and from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Creating and in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Creating and in clear steps. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Creating and in clear steps.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Creating and in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Creating and in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Creating and in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Creating and in one real-life situation this week.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Creating and” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Creating and in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Creating and is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Creating and” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain what Creating and means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Creating and in your own words. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Creating and from Kenya)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: practise Creating and in clear steps)

Example 4: Show how “Creating and” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: apply Creating and in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Creating and to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Creating and means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Creating and from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Creating and in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Creating and from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Creating and: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Creating and?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Creating and means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Creating and means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Creating and from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
